The Book of Revelation is found in the New Testament of the Bible, and it is specifically the final book of the New Testament [d7]. It begins with "The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave unto him, to shew unto his servants things which must shortly come to pass" (King James Version) [d3], and is also rendered in the NIV as "The revelation from Jesus Christ, which God gave him to show his servants what must soon take place" [d2]. The USCCB confirms it as a canonical biblical book containing visions in symbolic and allegorical language [d5], and it spans 22 chapters covering John's apocalyptic visions [d6]. While a minority of Christian organizations have questioned its inclusion in the New Testament canon [d4], the overwhelming consensus across traditions places it as the concluding book of the New Testament [d7][d5][d8].
